purpose: Attribute the Q4 1K-token prefill deficit on the M1 (jwm1-linux) without per-dispatch timestamp instrumentation, then screen the smallest digest-preserving schedule changes to the cooperative-matrix quantized matmul (tile geometry, k-step width, workgroup shape) at the real 1053-token Qwen2.5-0.5B shapes. Qualify source only if a repeatable digest-preserving gain exists; otherwise land a receipt-only negative.
question: Where does the 1K prefill token time go, and can the qmm coopmat schedule recover any of the 1113 vs 1840.9 tok/s deficit at the 1053-token leg?

source.change: Diagnostics-only: qmm_coopmat.comp parametrized over TILE_M {32,64} x STEP_K {16,32} and compiled four ways (three new CMake shader variants + append-only kernel enums QmmPrefillCoopmatM64F16/K32F16/M64K32F16 + MLX_OMARCHY_QMM_COOP_TILE selector, default 0). Default variant 0 SPIR-V is identical to the released kernel modulo ids (spirv-dis diff clean). Per-output k-accumulation order is preserved by construction in every variant: ascending 8-wide coopmat updates over k. The scaffolding is NOT landed; origin/main is untouched.

hardware.llvmpipe_screen: qmm coopmat host-reference test (18,384,704 assertions) passes on llvmpipe x86 before the M1 window; on llvmpipe the case runs the tile fallback (f32_8 unsupported there), matching receipts/2026-09-10-prefill-qmm-isa/targeted-llvmpipe.log

attribution.method: No per-dispatch timestamps. Component-isolated wall-time probes (median of 30 after 4 warmups) at the real shapes on the fork driver, reconciled against the whole-leg wall and the committed GPU-busy profile in receipts/2026-09-10-prefill-qmm-isa/conclusion.json.

attention_composite_sdpa.note: mx.fast.scaled_dot_product_attention composite (2x MatmulRbF16 + softmax + mask), 14 q heads / 2 kv heads / head_dim 64; its matmul kernels alone measured 109.4 ms in receipts/2026-09-10-prefill-qmm-isa

attribution.norms: rms_norm [1053,896] f16 = 0.387 ms per call; 48 model calls ≈ 18.6 ms
attribution.lm_head: full 1053x151936 logits would cost 267.6 ms and cannot fit the 946 ms leg together with the measured qmm; mlx_lm pays only the last-token slice (m=1 probe: 1.98 ms)
attribution.reconciliation: 726 (qmm) + 110 (attention matmuls) + softmax/rope/norms/elementwise ≈ 943 ms = the committed gpu_busy_ms at m1053; the remainder of the ~1004 ms span is submission/host overhead. The reconciliation matches receipts/2026-09-10-prefill-qmm-isa without any new instrumentation.

why_deficit_grows_with_context.mechanism: At m=30 the leg is latency/host-dominated for both platforms (fork qmm ≈ 40-45 ms of 90.6) and the fork is already past native. As context grows the leg becomes qmm-compute-bound, and there the fork's cooperative-matrix kernel saturates at ~1.03 TFLOP/s (40% of G13G f32 peak; 1028 GFLOP/s on gate_up, 974 on down_proj, 893 on q_proj at m=1053) while native Metal qmm sustains an implied ~1.7 TFLOP/s (whole native leg 572 ms minus attention/norms leaves ~430 ms for the 713 GFLOP of qmm work). The absolute deficit therefore grows from -12 ms at m=30 to +54 ms at m=262 to +374 ms at m=1053, tracking the qmm share, not the attention share (attention is quadratic but only 16% of the fork leg).

screen.method: Kernel-isolated quantized_matmul probe, f16 scales/biases (mx.quantize on f32, scales/biases cast f16), fixed seeds per shape, 4 warmups + 30 timed evals, median wall ms, f16 output sha256 per shape. Arms selected by MLX_OMARCHY_QMM_COOP_TILE. Repetition pass reran arms 0 and 1 twice more in alternating order under the same lock window.
screen.digest_gate: Every arm-0/arm-1 sample reproduced identical f16 output digests per shape across all repetitions (digest-preserving as designed). The committed probe-f16-scales digests are not comparable across probe scripts (different seeded inputs); arm-to-arm equality is the gate.
screen.repetition: Arms 0/1 rerun twice in alternation: base gate_up 17.83/17.85/17.90 ms (±0.2%), m64 gate_up 18.28/18.35/18.45 ms. The m64 regression on the dominant shape repeats in every sample.

verdicts.m64 (TILE_M 64, 128-lane 4-subgroup work: Digest-preserving, but -2.7% on gate_up (the shape that dominates the leg), neutral on down_proj and q_proj, not-better on the starved 128-wide shape. Rejected: halves per-workgroup weight re-reads and dequant work as designed, yet the 128-thread workgroup reduces independent workgroups and does not raise the kernel's ~1.03 TFLOP/s ceiling.
verdicts.k32 (STEP_K 32): -40 to -50% on every shape AND it changed the f16 output digest, which the source-level schedule analysis forbids (per-output k order is identical). Both facts disqualify it; the digest change is recorded as an empirical Honeykrisp cooperative-matrix anomaly worth remembering (wider k staging changed results that only reorder identically-ordered updates), not as an arithmetic improvement.
verdicts.m64_k32: Slow as k32 on the big shapes; digest matched base while k32 alone did not, an internally inconsistent driver-level result. Rejected.

decision: reject all three schedule variants; land no runtime source change
policy_ok: trivially: no source change, no digest movement, both drivers untouched
next: The remaining deficit is inside the coopmat kernel's achieved FLOP/s (Honeykrisp 8x8x8 emulation + the f32 shared-memory round trip for dequantized weights). On a quiet run the 946 ms leg is almost entirely GPU busy (wall ≈ the committed 943 ms gpu_busy), so host pacing is not the m1053 lever. Tile geometry and k-step width are exhausted by this screen; a future candidate must restructure the kernel's data path the way native Metal does (simdgroup dequant without the f32 shared round trip) - a new design, not a schedule tweak.
